memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If they dedicate a field after the Jubilee, the priest will determine
the value according to the number of years that remain until the next
Year of Jubilee, and its set value will be reduced. If the one who
dedicates the field wishes to redeem it, they must add a fifth to its
value, and the field will again become theirs'" - Lev 27:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The value of a dedicated field depended on how many years remained until
the Jubilee, when land returned to its family. Fewer years left meant a
lower value. God's instructions were precise, fair, and never arbitrary.

This care for accurate valuation tells us something about God's
character. He is not careless or approximate. He deals justly, taking
every relevant factor into account. There is no unfairness in Him.

Dear friend, we can trust a God who is this precise and this fair. When
life feels chaotic and outcomes seem random, it is steadying to remember
that we serve a God of perfect justice, who overlooks nothing and
miscalculates nothing.

Abraham asked, will not the Judge of all the earth do right? (Gen 18:25).
The answer running through all Scripture is yes. God will never treat you
unfairly. He sees every factor in your situation that others miss.

Notice too the recurring provision to redeem — to buy back what was
dedicated. Again and again this chapter offers a way back. God builds
second chances into His law, just as He builds them into His grace.

If you have ever feared that God might deal harshly or unfairly with you,
let these careful, just valuations reassure you. The God behind them can
be trusted completely with your life.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God deals fairly and justly with me?
2. Where do I need to rest in God's perfect fairness rather than fear?
3. How does God's precision and justice comfort me today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, You are perfectly just and never careless. When life feels
chaotic, help me rest in the truth that the Judge of all the earth always
does right. Amen.
